subject: Private Offer: dual-cloud pricing + partner margin routing (risk-share request)
messages:
From: Jake Simmons <jake@cloudnimbus.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer: dual-cloud bundle + channel margin routing question

Hannah —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. CloudNimbus is keen to move forward with a private offer, but we need to iron out two things before procurement will sign:

1) We want a single private offer that covers both AWS and GCP consumption (same SKU family), with clear list vs net pricing for each cloud.
2) Our channel team needs to know how the reseller margin will be passed through — we prefer a direct reseller passback (on invoice) rather than Redwood adjusting list price.

Procurement asked if Redwood can do a risk-share structure: if usage exceeds the commit by >25% in Q1, Redwood will provide a partial rebate to CloudNimbus and allow a larger reseller margin for that quarter. Is that something you can propose?

Can you put together a price table and an ops flow for passback so we can review with finance next week?

Regards,
Jake Simmons
Director, Cloud Strategy
CloudNimbus

Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer: dual-cloud bundle + channel margin routing question

Jake —

Great to hear — and thanks for the clear asks. We can definitely produce a single private offer that maps to AWS and GCP SKUs with a single contractual commitment. A few quick clarifying points before we model scenarios:

- The reseller passback can be handled either (A) as a line-item credit on Redwood invoices to CloudNimbus (pass-through), or (B) by mapping a higher list price and paying the reseller separately. Ops prefers option A for auditability.
- For the risk-share rebate: we can structure a Q1 overage rebate (sliding scale) but want to limit exposure. Typical structure is: 25-50% over commit => 20% rebate on incremental usage; >50% => cap at X. We should define the cap and exact percentages.
- Need partner routing diagram and invoice samples; I'll loop finance/ops.

I'll draft a price table and a channel routing stub and share by EOD Friday. Ben — can you run margin impact with Laura for option A vs B?

Cheers,
Hannah
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Hannah / team —

I ran a quick model for both passback options. High-level findings:

- Option A (invoice line-item pass-through): clean for partner, low operational friction on our end if we use a standard ledger credit. The downside: Redwood shows lower net revenue but retains gross list price for marketplace analytics.
- Option B (inflate list price + pay reseller): preserves our net revenue recognition but requires us to manage reseller payouts and withholdings (more billing ops work).

Margin impact (ballpark, per 1M list across both clouds):
- Option A: Redwood recognized revenue ~ $820k (reseller margin passed-through 18%), gross $1M
- Option B: Redwood recognized revenue ~ $900k (we pay reseller out of our gross), gross $1.08M list implied

On the risk-share rebate: if we commit to a Q1 rebate, suggest a tiered cap: incremental rebate at 20% for 25-50% overage up to $150k, then 10% beyond that up to a hard cap of $300k. That keeps expected exposure limited and scales with usage.

Laura — can you confirm billing/AR can handle an invoice credit flow and produce a sample invoice that shows a pass-through? Vivek — is this passback approach acceptable for channel partners from a legal/partner program perspective?

thanks,
Ben
Director, Deals
Redwood Inference

Jake / team —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is a draft private offer price table and a short ops diagram for the reseller passback (see attachments). High-level proposal:

- Single private offer covering matched SKUs on AWS and GCP. List price (per unit) is the same; net price shown per cloud can differ based on list->net mapping.
- Reseller passback handled as an invoice credit (Option A). Redwood issues credit memo referencing CloudNimbus PO and partner ID each month.
- Risk-share rebate (Q1 only) as suggested by Ben: 25-50% over commit => 20% rebate on incremental usage capped cumulatively at $150k; >50% => additional 10% rebate on remaining incremental usage up to a hard cap of $300k total. Rebate payable as invoice credit after Q1 close, conditional on monthly usage feeds and mutual audit.

Next steps:
- If this structure looks ok, we'll convert the draft XLS into a DocuSign-ready private offer and feed it into the marketplace private-offer flow (we'll need CloudNimbus's partner tax ID and signer).
- Ben / Laura: please confirm final numbers and the invoice sample are attached as promised.

Jake — can you share the partner tax ID and confirm CloudNimbus is okay with an invoice credit flow vs list-mapping? If procurement wants the other model, we can produce the alternative but it will take ops a bit longer.

Best,
Hannah
